oneLiner: A 27%-growth ad franchise valued like a value stock because the market doubts the $130-145B superintelligence capex bet will earn a return.
thesis: Ad machine still accelerating. Q2 2026 ad revenue rose 27% YoY to $59.4B with impressions +14% and price per ad +12% - AI is lifting volume and pricing simultaneously.
AI monetization is already revenue. Advantage+ reached a $75B annualized run-rate and 9M small businesses use Meta's AI ad-creative tools.

Unmatched distribution. 3.60B people use a Meta app daily, giving any new AI product instant global scale; FoA other revenue crossed $1B/quarter (+73% YoY) on WhatsApp paid messaging and subscriptions.

Superintelligence optionality. Muse Spark (April 2026) is MSL's first frontier model, now distributed via public API; Zuckerberg says compute demand far exceeds supply, implying monetization options beyond ads.
Valuation already derated. ~17x forward earnings, below its 5-year average and second-cheapest Mag 7; median street target $800.

latestProse: Q2 2026 revenue was $60.8B, +28% YoY, with ads at $59.4B (+27%) on impressions +14% and pricing +12%. Operating margin compressed to 31% from 43% as expenses jumped 55% to $42.0B - including $2.4B of unspecified legal accruals and $1.18B severance from ~8,000 AI-pivot layoffs - and EPS fell 13% to $6.18, the first miss in seven quarters. Reality Labs lost $4.62B on $431M revenue; FoA earned $23.4B. The disclosure that matters most: capex of $31.1B drove free cash flow down ~91% to $784M - the AI buildout is consuming nearly all cash generation.
guidanceProse: Q3 2026 revenue is guided to $61-64B. Full-year 2026 capex guidance was raised at the low end to $130-145B (from $125-145B), with another ramp signaled for 2027 (2027 range unverified). The debate: bulls say verified AI ad returns (Advantage+ $75B run-rate) fund the buildout; bears see FCF near zero, a 2027 depreciation wave, and a Superintelligence Labs program whose payback is unproven.

guide.label: 2026 capex guide
guide.sub: low end raised $5B in July; Q2 free cash flow just $784M

segments: Family of Apps: $60.4B revenue (99.3% of total), $23.4B operating income; other revenue >$1B (+73%) on WhatsApp paid messaging/subscriptions
Reality Labs: $431M (~0.7%), -$4.62B operating loss; pivoting from Quest VR toward AI glasses
competitive: Digital ads: duopoly with Google; Amazon scaling retail media; TikTok remains the engagement rival for Reels (current share splits unverified)
AI assistants: Meta AI's captive distribution vs ChatGPT and Gemini; Muse Spark and the 'Avocado' frontier project target GPT-6/Claude-class rivals
Open models: shift from open Llama to a hybrid/closed strategy cedes some open-weights leadership
Wearables: Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses lead consumer AI hardware
moat: 3.6B daily users and the deepest commercial-intent dataset outside Google feed self-reinforcing ad-targeting models rivals cannot replicate at scale. Advantage+'s $75B run-rate shows the AI flywheel converting into pricing power, and ~$60B/quarter of revenue funds a compute arms race few can match.
risks: Capex crushes free cash flow. $130-145B of 2026 capex took Q2 FCF to $784M (-91%); the depreciation wave hits 2027 margins.
Cost discipline broke. Expenses +55%, margins -12pts, first EPS miss in seven quarters.

Regulatory pincer. FTC is appealing its November 2025 monopolization loss (Instagram/WhatsApp breakup risk revived); a multistate youth-safety trial opened in Oakland in August 2026 with reported penalty demands up to $1.4T; EU DSA preliminary findings on minors carry fines of up to 6% of global revenue.
Superintelligence execution risk. MSL reorg churn, 8,000 layoffs and mercenary talent costs; Muse Spark must reach frontier parity or the spend is stranded.
Reality Labs still burns $4.6B/quarter, with the VR retreat producing write-downs, not savings.
Concentration: ~98% of revenue is advertising - an ad-market downturn hits everything at once.
catalysts: Aug 2026: multistate youth-safety trial underway in federal court, Oakland
Sept 23-24, 2026: Meta Connect, Menlo Park - new smart glasses teased
Late Oct 2026: Q3 2026 earnings - next capex/FCF read
Through 2026-27: FTC appeal briefing at the D.C. Circuit; EU DSA final decision on minors
pricedIn: At $599.12 (Aug 11, 2026), META trades ~20-22x trailing and ~17x forward consensus - below its 5-year average forward multiple and second-cheapest Mag 7 after Alphabet; median analyst target is $800. The price capitalizes the ad business and assigns little or negative value to AI/RL spend. The Aug 2026 debate: is the FCF trough a transitory investment cycle, as Advantage+'s run-rate suggests, or a structurally lower-return, capital-intensive Meta?

scenarios.bear: Ad growth decelerates toward mid-teens into 2027 while depreciation from $130B+ capex compresses margins further, and legal outcomes (youth-safety verdict, EU fines, FTC appeal) add multi-billion charges. EPS stagnates, the multiple holds ~15x: stock $450-500.
scenarios.base: Ads keep compounding ~20%+, margins trough in 2027 then recover as WhatsApp, API and AI ad revenue scale and capex peaks as a share of revenue. FCF inflects, the multiple re-rates toward ~20x forward: $650-720.
scenarios.bull: Muse Spark reaches frontier parity, compute monetization and business agents open non-ad revenue, and glasses hit a consumer inflection at Connect while ads grow >25%. META re-rates as an AI platform at 25x+, clearing the $800 target toward $900+.

valPresets.note: Basis is forward earnings: TTM FCF is crushed by the $130-145B capex program (Q2 FCF $784M), so an FCF-DCF would misread the investment cycle as value destruction.
